thread:
Maya: hey team, new hire here. trying to build the inference runtime from source on an Ubuntu WSL2 distro. nvcc reports 11.8, toolkit in /usr/local/cuda-11.8, but final link fails: undefined reference to `cublasLtSgemm` and libcuda.so.1 not found at runtime. quick guidance?

Jasper: welcome! :wave: first step: can you run `nvidia-smi` inside WSL? if that fails, the Windows-side driver for WSL might be missing. Also check where libcuda actually is with `find / -name "libcuda.so*" 2>/dev/null`.

Maya: `nvidia-smi` errors out with "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver." on the distro, but the Windows host shows the GPU fine. I installed the toolkit in the distro only.

Lin: yep that's the common pitfall. Install the NVIDIA Windows driver that includes WSL support (the one labeled WSL). After installing, restart Windows and then `wsl --shutdown` to restart the distro. Then `nvidia-smi` should work in WSL.

Maya: installed and restarted WSL. `nvidia-smi` now works. `find` shows `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1`. but ldconfig -p doesn't list libcuda. linking still fails with "cannot find -lcuda".

Jasper: if ldconfig doesn't list it, the simplest is to add the driver lib path to ld.so: create a file `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/nvidia-wsl.conf` containing `/usr/lib/wsl/lib`, then run `sudo ldconfig`. Alternatively create a symlink into `/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64`.

Maya: added conf and ran ldconfig. ldconfig -p now lists libcuda.so.1. build moves past cublasLt but fails later with undefined reference to `cuGetProcAddress`.

Lin: `cuGetProcAddress` is added in newer CUDA driver APIs. Check that the libcuda reported by `ldconfig -p` actually exports that symbol: `nm -D /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuGetProcAddress`. If it's missing, you need a driver update. If present, the linker order might be wrong.

Maya: nm shows the symbol present. link command in logs: `g++ -o libruntime.so ... -L/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64 -lcudart -lcublas -lcublasLt -l:libcuda.so.1`. still undefined refs.

Jasper: try moving `-l:libcuda.so.1` after the other libs or use `-Wl,--start-group` and `--end-group` around them. Linkers resolve symbols left-to-right. Example: `-Wl,--start-group -lcublasLt -lcublas -lcudart -l:libcuda.so.1 -Wl,--end-group`. Also verify your build isn't linking against a stub `libcuda` from the toolkit rather than the real driver lib. `readelf -s /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuGetProcAddress` should be good.

Maya: reordering to put libcuda last fixed the link errors. thank you. final hurdle: when running the test suite inside a docker container (built with CUDA base image), the container complains /dev/nvidia0 permission denied. I tried mounting /dev with `-v /dev:/dev` but that feels wrong.

Lin: on WSL + Docker Desktop, you should enable WSL integration in Docker Desktop settings and install `nvidia-container-toolkit` in the distro so the runtime can create device nodes. Use `--gpus all` in `docker run` and check docker daemon config `/etc/docker/daemon.json` contains the NVIDIA runtime default. Also check the container sees `/dev/nvidiactl` and `/dev/nvidia-uvm` inside.

Maya: after enabling integration and installing the toolkit the container starts but inside the runtime `cudaGetDeviceCount` returns 0. `ls -l /dev/nvidia*` on the host shows devices owned by root with group `video` and mode 600. my user is in `docker` but not `video`.

Jasper: add your user to the `video` group or adjust udev rules for device permissions. `sudo usermod -aG video $USER` then logout/login of the distro (or `newgrp video`) should let the container access devices properly. For CI, we usually run a helper that `chgrp video /dev/nvidia* && chmod g+rw /dev/nvidia*` at startup.

infra-bot: note: to avoid permission issues in CI, prefer using GPU-enabled runner images with preconfigured nvidia runtime instead of mounting host devices manually.

Maya: added myself to video group and restarted the distro. `cudaGetDeviceCount` now returns 1 inside the container, and full test run passes locally. I'll add a short onboarding note to the eng-runtime README covering: required Windows driver, ld.so conf entry, preferred link order for -lcuda, and Docker Desktop + nvidia-container-toolkit steps. thanks all! :sparkles:
